meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_138_packages.json (proposed packages), all reference===138 edges from torahData.js (ZERO found), and the full source text torah_138.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset (torahData.js) and whether it is assigned to a package. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בִּבְחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, לְשׁוֹן) or direct identity statements (הוּא, הֵם) in the Rebbe's voice were considered. Since the entire Torah is unencodeded, all concepts qualify as gaps.

additions.reason: The Rebbe introduces בַּר לֵבָב (Ps. 24:4 — 'pure/empty of heart') as the positive human subject of this Torah. The one who is bar levav is the person who can receive divine speech through the heart. The explicit bechina in this Torah is: 'בַּר לֵבָב בִּבְחִינַת וְלִבִּי חָלַל בְּקִרְבִּי' — the quality of being bar levav IS, in its essential nature, the hollow heart. This is the primary bechina edge of this Torah. Not currently in the dataset for reference 138.

additions.reason: The hollow/emptied heart ('my heart is hollow within me', Ps. 109:22) is the bechina-counterpart of בַּר לֵבָב. The Rebbe uses this verse to define what it means to be 'pure of heart': the heart must be emptied of self in order to become a transparent vessel for divine speech. Hollowness here is a positive spiritual quality — the precondition for receiving the word of God through the heart. This is the target node in the Torah's central bechina edge.

additions.reason: The heart (לֵב) is the central concept of this Torah. The Rebbe states directly: 'כִּי עִקַּר הָאֱלֹקוּת – בַּלֵּב' — the essence of divinity is in the heart. This is an identity statement (not a bechina with bichnat language, but a declarative 'X is in Y' that functions as equivalence in Rebbe Nachman's discourse). The heart appears as the hub connecting divine presence, divine speech, and the human subject who has hollowed himself. It is the dominant node of Package 1 by virtue of being the central concept mentioned repeatedly.

proposed_edge.proof: כִּי עִקַּר הָאֱלֹקוּת – בַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: צוּר לְבָבִי

additions.reason: The 'essence of divinity' (עִקַּר הָאֱלֹקוּת) is declared to be located in the heart. This is the theological foundation of the Torah: God's essential presence resides in the heart, not merely as metaphor but as a substantive claim backed by the verse 'צוּר לְבָבִי' (God is the Rock of my heart). The Rebbe cross-references Torah #49 for this teaching, indicating it is a major principle in his system. As a concept, עִקַּר הָאֱלֹקוּת is the bechina-equivalent of לֵב within this teaching.

additions.reason: The 'actual/literal words of God' (דִּבְרֵי ה' מַמָּשׁ) is the identity given to what the heart speaks. The Rebbe states this twice with emphasis: 'שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי ה' מַמָּשׁ' and 'כִּי מַה שֶּׁהַלֵּב אוֹמֵר, הֵם דִּבְרֵי ה' מַמָּשׁ'. This is the functional equivalent/bechina of the heart's speech: what the heart says IS the divine word. The word מַמָּשׁ (literally, actually) emphasizes the non-metaphorical identity. This concept is the bechina-complement of לֵב in the teaching's core equation.

additions.reason: Knowing the future (יְדִיעַת עֲתִידוֹת) is the eitza-result of being bar levav with a hollow heart: 'יוּכַל לֵידַע עֲתִידוֹת, עַל־יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁהַלֵּב אוֹמֵר לוֹ'. The construction 'עַל־יְדֵי' marks this as a causal consequence (eitza), not a shared-nature equivalence (bechina). Prophetic foreknowledge flows FROM the heart receiving divine speech; it is not the same thing as the heart or the divine speech. Belongs in Package 2 as a standalone eitza-result node, representing the practical spiritual gift that is the culmination of this Torah's teaching.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 3 cites the verse 'צוּר לְבָבִי' (Ps. 73) as proof that God is the Rock of the heart. This is a scriptural proof-text supporting the identity of לֵב with עִקַּר הָאֱלֹקוּת. The Rebbe does NOT use 'בִּבְחִינַת' for this — he says 'כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב' (as it is written), which is a citation of evidence, not an establishment of a new bechina node. Excluded as proof-text, not a standalone bechina.

The Rebbe explains 'לְךָ' as meaning 'בִּשְׁלִיחוּתְךָ' (in Your commission). This is Rashi's bechina, cited by the Rebbe. The Rebbe adopts it ('כַּנַּ"ל' — as said above). The node בִּשְׁלִיחוּתְךָ captures this concept; 'לְךָ' by itself is merely the verse fragment that prompted it. Not listed separately.

Line 3 says 'כַּמְבֹאָר אֶצְלֵנוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר (לעיל בסימן מט)' — as we have explained elsewhere (above in section 49). This is a cross-reference, not a bechina in Torah #138. Torah #49's elaboration of the heart-divinity teaching belongs in Torah #49's package system, not here.
